blocks.note: first meaning: read as the phrasal verb, to tear away
second meaning: a swindle or con

explanation.surface: A young hooligan who is also a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearaway' looks like the noun for a reckless youth, but it is split as the verb phrase 'tear away', which a hyphenated three-and-three phrase can also mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle that overcharges someone is colloquially called this, and the same phrase as a verb means to pull something off forcibly.

indicators.note: something sullied has been messed up, so the letters before it are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grime in an engine has fouled one of its components.
explanation.definitionFit: One component of a recipe or mixture is called this, so the word is a synonym for a constituent part.

clue.text: Am I a more reliable ruler?

definitions.text: Am I a more reliable ruler?

blocks.clueFragment: Am I a more reliable ruler?
blocks.note: surface reading: a monarch wondering whether they govern more dependably than others
setter's reading: a ruler is a device for gauging length, and the riddle asks what that device calls itself

explanation.surface: A king or queen anxiously asks whether they are a steadier sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ME A SURER, the answer literally says 'me, a more reliable one', which is why the clue is phrased as a question about oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edged ruler is a tool for taking lengths, so it is one that measures things.

clue.text: French woman turned to follow German

indicators.note: turned means spun round to face the other way, so the name is written back to front
to follow places this piece after the other one in the answer

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for German
a woman's name, as in the singer and TV presenter Cilla Black

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman changes sides and goes after a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French woman' reads as one phrase, but 'French' is the definition on its own; the woman is CILLA, written backwards after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaul was the Roman name for the region that became France, so this adjective is a common synonym for French.

clue.text: Finally taking rap, American pleaded and fought

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: the last letter of taking
taken as written
pled is the American past tense of plead

explanation.surface: An American, at last accepting the blame, made a plea and then resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the rap means to accept punishment, which makes the surface read like a courtroom story.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle or struggle at close quarters with an opponent is a synonym for having fought.

blocks.note: la is a French word for 'the'
to cross someone is to thwart or obstruct them
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: French players stand in the way of an English sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with netted sticks, it is a specific example of a game.

clue.text: Give rise to a bit of energetic sex

indicators.note: a bit of means only a small opening portion of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the first two letters of energetic
gender is a synonym for sex as a category

explanation.surface: A spot of vigorous lovemaking leads to new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' reads as the act in the surface but is used in its other sense, a category of male or female.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause or bring about a feeling or situation is a formal synonym for giving rise to it.

indicators.note: concealing says the words before it keep something tucked away inside them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone arrived in Ripon with drugs hidden on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire. 'dope' suggests drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, dull or foolish person is called this colloquially, much as an idiot is called a dope.

indicators.note: pointless means without a compass point, so one such letter is dropped
wild means out of control, so the remaining letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; N, for north, is the compass point to lose

explanation.surface: Pure fury, uncontrolled and without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' looks like 'futile' but means minus a point of the compass: here N.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent, uncontrolled fury is a close synonym for anger, used both as a noun and a verb.

clue.text: Fix article to church door? Do leave it out!

indicators.note: leave it out tells us to omit the word Do from the word just before

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written before it loses two letters

explanation.surface: Should a notice be nailed to the church door? Please don't.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Luther nailing theses to a church door; 'Leave it out!' is also British slang for 'stop it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something firmly in place is to fix it, as a ship is held fast by its heavy weight.

blocks.note: Pres is a short form of president
to sing is slang for confessing to police

explanation.surface: A pushy head of state is made to own up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing' as underworld slang means to inform or confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Importunate means persistently demanding, and a demand that will not wait is urgent and insistent in the same way.

clue.text: Poorer fared badly? He corrects inaccurate impression

indicators.note: badly means done poorly, so the preceding letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who did worse fixes a false picture of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impression' is a print run from type, so an inaccurate impression is a misprint rather than a wrong belief.
explanation.definitionFit: This person checks printed proofs and marks errors, correcting a faulty print before publication.

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
O looks like zero
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: The electorate opts for no taxes at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British local property tax before the council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of people entitled to vote in an election is a collective term for voters.

clue.text: Fixed due price for bunion treatment?

indicators.note: fixed here means rigged or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A set fee owed for treating a foot complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a bunion is just one thing such care deals with.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic and medical care of the feet and toenails would include attention to a bunion on the big toe.

indicators.note: adulterated means corrupted by mixing, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: Spiked cannabis may leave a smoker dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is slang for cannabis, which makes the surface about a doped joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural form names a disease of sheep and horses and, informally, a fit of dizziness or unsteadiness.

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the six letters of scenes plus the extra e, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild landscapes are being ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nature' looks like the countryside of the surface, but it is the definition in the sense of a thing's basic character.
explanation.definitionFit: The intrinsic, fundamental character of something is its nature, a close synonym.

blocks.note: taken as written
something not late is punctual

explanation.surface: Someone insists that it isn't late after all, it's only twelve o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the day, the hour of noon, is another word for midday.

clue.text: Serious attention given to North-east's predicament at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before
given to means the following pieces are added after the first one

blocks.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
NE is north-east, plus the S of the possessive
the last letter of predicament

explanation.surface: Finally, the plight of England's North East is getting serious consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and intensely serious in manner or intention, the adjective is a direct synonym for serious.

clue.text: Prominent, openly gay and up for election

blocks.note: someone out has publicly declared their sexuality
a candidate stands for election

explanation.surface: A high-profile candidate who is openly gay is running for office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stands out from the rest is conspicuous or striking, a synonym for prominent.

indicators.note: dropping names means letting two letters standing for name fall away
indiscriminately means at random, so the letters are thrown into any order

blocks.note: taken as written; N is the abbreviation for name, and two of its Ns go

explanation.surface: Watch an innocent party being careless about who gets mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping names' looks like name-dropping, but means removing two letters N, each standing for name.
explanation.definitionFit: To see or become aware of something is to observe it, and the verb is used in exactly that sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: a score of zero in tennis
second meaning: to be fond of, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing like' reads as one phrase meaning 'not at all similar', but it breaks into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a score of zero is called this, and as a verb it means to be very fond of something.

blocks.note: first meaning: to bombard with blows or missiles
second meaning: an animal's hide with its fur

explanation.surface: Keep hitting and then flay the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hurl things at someone again and again; as a noun it is an animal's furry hide.

blocks.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money
a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: Someone is bothered by media spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as 'annoyed' but is the verb meaning to knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something over or reverse a ruling is to upset it, as in upsetting a boat or a verdict.

clue.text: Get accustomed to initially almost toxic air

indicators.note: initially means at the start, keeping only the opening letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: Learning to live with air that is nearly poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' reads as the atmosphere but is used in its musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring into harmony or make receptive is to adjust oneself, so getting used to something fits closely.

clue.text: Form opinion of terminally tense state I'm in

indicators.note: terminally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used
in places the preceding piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the last letter of tense
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone judges how anxious and terminally ill they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminally tense' suggests chronic anxiety, but 'terminally' just picks the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an approximate judgement or assessment of something's value or size is to form an opinion of it.

clue.text: Gain admittance to a cricket club, Essex mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the end of the word is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
taken as written; Essex is an English county

explanation.surface: Trying to get into a cricket club, most of which is in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county just east of London with a famous county cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to reach or enter, so obtaining entry to a place or system is this word.
